answer.rationale: Competitive price pressure on SMB creates urgency, but memory_73 explicitly warns that promotional_pricing reduces 30-day retention materially and should not be generalized as growth strategy. This rules out direct pricing response. Memory_31 and memory_86 show signup simplification and shortened onboarding drive activation and retention gains; memory_91 demonstrates activation messaging improves week-one engagement. A layered approach using activation_messaging as the primary lever (memory_91: nudge accounts to first meaningful action) combined with the proven onboarding improvements from memory_86 addresses the core problem: increasing perceived value and time-to-value faster than competitors can undercut on price. Referral_incentives (memory_57) work well in established customers but do not address acute churn in price-sensitive SMB cohort. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB pressure. Standard_experiment allows rapid deployment to price-sensitive cohorts while preserving ability to measure retention impact before broad rollout. This preserves long-term qualified revenue by increasing stickiness and activation rather than eroding margins or unit economics.
